 # `comptime(expr)`: evaluate a constant expression at compile time and replace
 # it with its literal (the Zig model). The evaluator is a PURE SANDBOX:
 # literals, arithmetic, boolean and comparison operators only.
 def table_size() Int64 := comptime(2 + 3 * 4)           # becomes the literal 14
 def scaled() Int64     := comptime((1 + 2) * 5)          # becomes 15
-def always() Bool    := comptime(3 > 5)                # becomes false
+def always() Bool      := comptime(3 > 5)                # becomes false

@@ -44,3 +48,20 @@ def always() Bool    := comptime(3 > 5)                # becomes false
 #
 # There is no build-time effect without an explicit (and currently deferred)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# PORTABLE-CORE DISCIPLINE (ADR-0035 no-hidden-control-flow · ADR-0058)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# In a `@targets(…)` module — code promised to compile to every listed target —
+# a macro may NOT introduce caller-invisible control flow. A template that
+# expands a one-line call site into a failable bind (`with … <- …`, ADR-0039)
+# is rejected at compile time, because the error a reader would have to debug
+# points at expanded nodes they never wrote ("debugging a ghost"). For example,
+# inside `@targets(ex, rs, js) mod …` this macro is refused:
+#
+#   macro unwrap(e) := with {:ok, v} <- e do v end
+#                      # ^ rejected: "introduces a failable bind … not allowed
+#                      #   in portable/@targets code"
+#
+# Outside a `@targets` module the same macro is allowed — the discipline binds
+# exactly the code that claims to be portable, nothing more.
